biography_sections.title: Monument and dates
biography_sections.markdown: The [family monument transcription](https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up), published in *Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim*, *Ulster Journal of Archaeology*, second series 6 (1900), p.47, names Mary as daughter of William and Elizabeth and gives death **18 October 1844 aged 37**. Birth about 1807 is calculated from that age. The uncertain Larne death place is inferred, not explicitly stated by the inscription.

biography_sections.title: Possible duplicate: the 1843 bride
biography_sections.markdown: [Mary Glasgow-4181](/people/glasgow-4181.html), the bride in the [1843 settlement](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-FQ3Q), is a possible duplicate of this Mary. Her probable census identification gives death in autumn 1843 aged 37, conflicting with this Mary’s monument death 18 October 1844 aged 37. Separate profiles remain provisional. The new bride’s uncertain attachment to Hugh Glasgow-4180 does not displace this Mary’s monument-proved father William Glasgow-3324; if the women are identical, the Hugh hypothesis must be withdrawn.

death.note: Exact death date from published family monument; death location inferred.

opening: Mary, daughter of William Glasgow and Elizabeth, died on 18 October 1844 aged 37, supporting birth about 1807. The 1843 bride Mary Glasgow-4181 remains a possible duplicate; her probable census identification has a conflicting 1843 death year.
